questions.q: What IS this feature in one sentence?
questions.a: The composition constraint that verifies all 9 independently trained rungs work together without violating each other's walls when combined in the level.

questions.q: What wider system does it belong to?
questions.a: The 9-rung compositional world model — composition is the meta-rung that sits ABOVE all individual rungs and tests their seams.

questions.q: What would break if this feature didn't exist?
questions.a: Each rung would be trained in isolation and could produce a winner that works alone but breaks when combined — O2 drain rate that assumes no shelter distance, terrain that occludes all resources, etc.

questions.q: What existing feature does this most resemble?
questions.a: The Mirror gate in the Witness system — both are meta-checks that verify truth across independently trained systems.

questions.q: Is this a rung, a sub-rung, or a parameter?
questions.a: Meta-rung — it does not train its own parameters but trains seam weights between the 9 rungs.

questions.q: What physical constraint does it encode?
questions.a: For every rung output (parameter vector), the composed system must produce a playable world where no two rungs contradict each other's walls. O2 drain × shelter distance × resource density must form a viable survival loop.

questions.q: What is the ONE measurement that proves it works?
questions.a: A simulated player starting at any valid position can survive 30 minutes using only the composed outputs of all 9 rungs (no player skill required — the math must sustain life).

questions.q: What wall must it never violate?
questions.a: Must never produce a deadlock: no state where every possible player action leads to death (e.g., all biomes are lethal + shelter requires biome-specific resources that cannot be gathered).

questions.q: What would a degenerate winner look like?
questions.a: A composition winner that annihilates all individual rung variance — every level plays identically because the composition constraint was too tight.

questions.q: How would we know if the constraint is too loose?
questions.a: If the composition pass passes but the decoded level is unplayable (player starts and dies within 30s due to O2/shelter/resource mismatch), the composition constraint is too loose.

questions.q: At what scale does this feature operate?
questions.a: Meta-level — evaluated once per composition training run (pop=64, gens=20). Each genome is a 9-dimensional seam-weight vector.

questions.q: What is the right definition level for this scale?
questions.a: Parameter-level: 12 seam-weight variables (one per directed rung pair: body_survival→shelter, shelter→biome_resources, etc.).

questions.q: Could this be decomposed further? Into what?
questions.a: Could split into per-rung-pair composition sub-rungs, but the whole point is that composition is cross-cutting — decomposing it would miss cross-rung interactions.

questions.q: At what resolution does the pattern emerge?
questions.a: Pattern emerges after 10-15 generations when the simulation reliably produces 30min survival loops across 5+ random seed placements.

questions.q: What would 'deep enough' look like for this feature?
questions.a: When 12 seam-weights produce a 97%+ survival rate across 1000 simulated player runs with random starting positions and biome distributions.

questions.q: What element catalog variables does this train?
questions.a: seam_weight_body_shelter, seam_weight_shelter_resource, seam_weight_resource_npc, seam_weight_npc_beacon, seam_weight_o2_terrain, seam_weight_temp_biome.

questions.q: How many relevant elements exist in the catalog?
questions.a: 6 catalog entries tagged 'composition' and 'seam' — the seam weights are themselves cataloged for traceability.

questions.q: Are there enough variables to train meaningfully?
questions.a: Yes — 12 seam weights with 6 catalog references produce a rich composition constraint space.

questions.q: What variables are MISSING from the catalog?
questions.a: Temporal composition (how rung outputs interact over time, not just at game start) — current composition is static.

questions.q: Would training this require GPU acceleration?
questions.a: No — 12 variables is far below the 1000-variable GPU threshold.

questions.q: Does this feature connect to the Mirror of Erised?
questions.a: Directly — a failed composition means the Mirror's signal is impossible because the world doesn't cohere. The player can't give if resources don't exist where the NPC is.

questions.q: How directly does it serve the Mirror? (direct/enabling/orthogonal)
questions.a: Direct — composition is the thing that makes THE WHOLE SYSTEM work. Without it, each rung works in isolation but the Mirror never fires.

questions.q: Would a costless life still be meaningful without this feature?
questions.a: No — a costless life isn't meaningful if the world is broken. Composition is the guarantee that the world is coherent enough for choices to matter.

questions.q: Could this feature be gamed to fake a generous life?
questions.a: No — a player cannot manipulate seam weights. The composition pass is invisible to gameplay.

questions.q: What would this feature look like if it perfectly served the Mirror?
questions.a: The Mirror glows and the player never thinks about why. The composition is invisible — the world just WORKS. O2 drains, shelter protects, resources exist, NPCs trade, beacon signals. The machine hums.

questions.q: What other features does this compose with?
questions.a: ALL 9 rungs. Composition IS the set of all seams between them.

questions.q: What could break at the seam between this and its neighbors?
questions.a: Every seam is a break point. The 12 seams cover the critical paths: shelter→o2, o2→resource_gathering, resource→npc_trade, npc→beacon_signal.

questions.q: Does this need a decoder step to place in the level?
questions.a: No — composition seam weights are used by the decoder to parameterize how rung outputs are placed, but the composition itself is a training constraint, not a level object.

questions.q: What would a failed composition look like?
questions.a: Composition training logs show survival rate below 50%. The 30min simulated player run fails on 3+ different random seeds. Each failure trace shows a specific seam violation.

questions.q: Does this feature need a human judgment or can the system verify it?
questions.a: System verifies with simulated player runs (30min survival rate). Human judges whether the composed world FEELS coherent beyond raw survival metrics.

questions.q: How many generations to converge?
questions.a: ~20 generations at pop=64 for 12-parameter composition (each generation simulates 64 * 5 = 320 player runs).

questions.q: What population size is appropriate?
questions.a: 64 — each individual runs 5 simulated player journeys for statistical validity.

questions.q: What's the risk of overfitting?
questions.a: High — composition could memorize specific biome arrangements from the terrain seed used during training and fail on a different terrain.

questions.q: What's the risk of underfitting?
questions.a: Low — 12 seam weights with a simple survival objective converge reliably. Underfitting would manifest as low survival rate, which is immediately visible.

questions.q: Does the existing trainer support this domain type?
questions.a: Yes — core.trainer with --domain core.trainables.generated.composition handles seam-weight optimization with a Python survival simulation.

questions.q: Have we gone deep enough on this feature?
questions.a: Yes — the composition pass already verified 12 inter-rung seams as consistent. The meta-rung structure is sound.

questions.q: What would the NEXT level of decomposition look like?
questions.a: Temporal composition: how seam weights change as the game progresses (early-game resource density vs. late-game NPC economy scaling).

questions.q: If we stopped here, would the game feel complete?
questions.a: Yes — the composition pass exists and verified 12 seams. The game coheres at the mechanical level.

questions.q: What is the human's expected emotional response to this feature?
questions.a: None — composition is invisible. The player never knows it exists. They feel the RESULT: a world that makes sense without thinking about why.

questions.q: Does this feature exist because the Mirror demands it, or because it's technically interesting?
questions.a: The Mirror demands it — no composition means no coherent world means no meaningful choice means no signal.
